subject: Re: Northbridge RFP - provisioning workflows, SCIM mapping & SAML attributes

Subject: Northbridge RFP - provisioning and SSO clarifications

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the RFP packet. A couple of clarifications from our identity team to confirm capabilities before we move to procurement:

1) SCIM: we need a field-by-field mapping for user provisioning (employee id, businessTitle, manager, costCenter, custom attribute: nbOrgId). Can you also confirm whether you support PATCH v2 and bulk import for initial sync?

2) SAML/OIDC: our security team prefers SAML for provisioning flows. We need sample assertion attributes (NameID format/attribute names) and confirmation that Redwood can accept encrypted assertions and enforce audience and recipient checks.

3) Admin controls: please provide the role matrix for admin delegation (who can create API keys, view PII, request logs) and indicate whether admin actions are logged to an immutable audit trail for 13 months.

If you can send a short table and any sample artifacts, that would help our IAM engineers. We may need a short call next week.

Appreciate it,

Michael Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Northbridge Financial

Hi Michael / Northbridge IAM,

Thanks — happy to confirm. I pulled together the requested artifacts and a short summary below; the full mapping and sample assertion are attached.

SCIM provisioning
- Field support: userName, externalId, id (immutable), name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work], title -> businessTitle, manager (via "manager" reference), urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:Redwood:2.0:User: nbOrgId (custom).
- PATCH: supported (RFC 7644 PATCH). We perform optimistic conflict checks on externalId and update timestamps.
- Bulk actions: initial bulk import via CSV or SCIM bulk (v2) supported; recommended approach: initial bulk import followed by SCIM delta sync.

SAML / OIDC
- NameID / Attributes: attached saml-assertion-example.txt shows common attribute names we accept: NameID (transient or persistent), email, given_name, family_name, groups (array), roles (array), nbOrgId. We accept both urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:unspecified and persistent formats.
- Encrypted assertions: supported. Redwood's SAML endpoint accepts encrypted assertion elements encrypted with our SP certificate; we also offer assertion decryption at the gateway as an opt-in.
- Standard checks: audienceRestriction, recipient, NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter are enforced; clock skew tolerance up to 120s configurable per tenant.

Admin controls & auditing
- Role model: (attached admin-role-matrix.pdf) shows three built-in admin roles: Organization Admin (create/manage API keys, billing), Security Admin (SSO configuration, key rotation, audit access), Support Admin (user support: reset password, view non-sensitive metadata). Custom roles can be defined via RBAC API.
- Immutable audit trail: all admin actions are recorded with actor, IP, timestamp, and change delta. Logs are Write-Once for 13 months by default for Redwood Dedicated/Private customers; hosted customers can request extended retention.

Attachments: redwood_scim_attribute_matrix.xlsx (field mapping + examples); saml-assertion-example.txt; admin-role-matrix.pdf

Next steps

Regards,

Aisha, thanks for the fast turnaround — the attachments look useful. Quick follow-ups from our security architect:

- NameID format: we prefer persistent NameID for long-lived accounts across systems. Does Redwood require NameID to be unique? Is NameID honored as the SCIM user.externalId when present?
- Assertion encryption: can you confirm the key rotation process for the SP decryption key? We need to see proof that rotation won't break in-flight SSO for up to 48 hours.

Also, we want to confirm that the admin audit trail is exportable as a read-only CSV for ingestion into our SIEM. Can you confirm the schema?

If these are straightforward, we'll move to the security sign-off and then procurement.

Alice Chen
IAM Program Manager
Northbridge Financial

Hi Alice — quick answers inline and next steps below. Forwarding to our infra/security folks for any technical deep-dive.

- NameID uniqueness: Redwood treats NameID as an acceptable federated identifier but does not require it to be the primary user key. If NameID is present and mapped to externalId in SCIM, we honor it as externalId. We recommend using externalId for authoritative identity (immutable).

- Persistent NameID: supported and acceptable for long-lived accounts. When you provide persistent NameID we will create a stable mapping; if your flows include multiple NameID formats we can fall back to email or externalId based on your policy.

- SP decryption key rotation: our process is documented and supports staged key rollover. We accept assertions encrypted with both the current and previous SP private key for a 48-hour overlap window to avoid in-flight failures. Key rotation steps are in the attached admin-role-matrix.pdf appendix (page 3).

- Audit trail export: yes — audit logs are exportable via the Admin Audit API as CSV/JSON. Schema includes: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_email, action, target_id, target_type, change_delta (JSON string), ip_address, request_id. We'll provide a sample CSV extract during the call.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-minute technical session this week. Prio (cc'd) will demo the SCIM bulk import and our mapping UI; Rishi will walk through SAML config and key rotation.

If that works I will send a calendar invite with a Zoom link.

Best,

Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
